note: Two ranking paths exist and both are scored. The semantic path is the production default; the positional path is the fallback when no embedding is available. Quoting one number for 'cross-repo MRR' would describe neither.

semantic.when: The caller supplies a query embedding and the items carry vectors. This is the default in production, because write-time embedding is on unless disabled.
semantic.scoring: Cosine against the query embedding, for local and peer candidates alike. Comparable across repos only because a workspace pins one embedding identity.
semantic.result: The weakness recorded against the positional path is resolved. xrepo-answer-elsewhere ranked the correct foreign answer second under reciprocal rank; cosine separates it from the weak local match on meaning and it ranks first, taking MRR from 0.833 to 1.0.
semantic.selection: Candidates are chosen vector-first and topped up lexically, mirroring the local union of vector and BM25 candidates. Selecting lexically alone would exclude any peer item sharing no query token, so cosine would never get to rank it.

positional.when: No query embedding, or items without vectors -- an unembedded repo, or a caller that did not compute one.
positional.scoring: One scoring pass over every repo's candidates together: absolute text-match strength, freshness, confidence, category and recency, plus a bounded reciprocal-rank term from each repo's own lexical position. Ties break toward the local repo.
positional.verifiedBy: tests/workspace/cross-repo-eval.test.ts (the suite runs with KNOWL_DISABLE_WRITE_EMBEDDING=1, so it measures this path)

resolvedWeakness.wasRecorded: 2026-07-27 at MRR 0.833. The correct answer ranked second: web's 'Web scratch note' mentions auth in passing and, as rank 1 of its own corpus, scored identically to server's rank-1 'Auth token TTL', so the local tie-break put the weaker local match first.
resolvedWeakness.why: The 2026-07-27 entry said raising this number 'means giving cross-corpus scores real comparability, which is the work the ablation exists to justify'. That work is done, and it removed the fusion rather than tuning it. Each repo is selected separately and every candidate is scored in one pass, so no item is ever 'rank 1 of its own corpus' relative to another. The dominant term is now absolute text-match strength (up to 0.2) rather than the corpus-relative rank term (at most ~0.016), and a passing mention no longer ties a direct answer.
resolvedWeakness.notTuned: No weight was added or changed. The improvement comes from deleting the fusion step, and the semantic path's numbers are unchanged, which is what rules out an accidental re-tune of the shared scorer.

positional.remainingCorpusRelativeTerm: bm25Rank is still each repo's own lexical position. It survives as a bounded fallback for candidates with no vector -- at most about 0.006 -- and is now outweighed by absolute terms rather than deciding the order.

invariants.comment: A peer's repo-private item must never appear on either path, however well it matches.
